title: Beyond Single-Pathogen Forecasts: Predicting Shared Respiratory Hospital Burden from Influenza, COVID-19, and RSV
abstract: arXiv:2610.16074v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Co-circulating influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) create a shared hospital-admission burden, because beds, staff, testing capacity, and respiratory support are allocated to total demand rather than to one pathogen at a time. This makes respiratory forecasting a target-construction problem as well as a modeling problem: disease-specific forecasts preserve attribution, whereas hospitals also need a single planning signal for combined burden. We developed a supervised 1- to 4-week-ahead framework for weekly admissions and compared two total-burden strategies: summing independently generated pathogen-specific forecasts and forecasting the combined admission target directly. translated_title: 超越单一病原体预测：基于流感、COVID-19和呼吸道合胞病毒预测共享的呼吸道住院负担
translated_abstract: 流感、COVID-19和呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）的共同流行造成了共享的医院入院负担，因为床位、工作人员、检测能力和呼吸支持设备是按照总需求而非单一病原体需求来分配的。这使得呼吸道预测既是一个目标构建问题，也是一个建模问题：针对特定疾病的预测保留了病原体归因信息，而医院还需要一个针对综合负担的统一规划信号。我们开发了一个监督式的未来1至4周每周入院人数预测框架，并比较了两种总负担预测策略：将独立生成的针对特定病原体的预测结果相加，以及直接对联合入院目标进行预测。评估包括回顾性留出测试和在观察到相应入院周之前发布的前瞻性业务预测，性能用平均绝对误差（MAE）和百分比一致率（PA；模型生成的较小值……）来总结。
tldr: 该研究开发了针对流感、新冠和RSV共同流行的1至4周呼吸道住院总量预测框架，并比较了“分别预测各病原体后求和”与“直接预测联合入院目标”两种策略，为医院提供了统一的住院负担规划信号。
en_tdlr: This study develops a supervised 1- to 4-week-ahead forecasting framework for combined influenza, COVID-19, and RSV hospital admissions, comparing summing pathogen-specific forecasts versus directly forecasting the combined burden to provide hospitals a unified planning signal.
